claims.text: Maintaining the powder-bed-fusion build chamber at approximately 600°C will reduce thermal gradients across successive AlCrFeNiSi layers.
Build-chamber preheating will produce a more uniform temperature distribution during layer deposition.
A more uniform temperature distribution will minimize rapid thermal cycling.
Reduced thermal gradients and thermal cycling will lower residual thermal stresses in AlCrFeNiSi miniature components.
Build-chamber preheating will mitigate microstructural degradation in AlCrFeNiSi.
Microstructural degradation caused by rapid thermal cycles leads to inferior mechanical properties.
Components produced with approximately 600°C chamber preheating will have greater tensile strength than components produced by powder bed fusion without chamber preheating.
Components produced with approximately 600°C chamber preheating will have longer fatigue life than components produced by powder bed fusion without chamber preheating.
Adding chamber preheating will simplify processing relative to conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing.
The proposed processing window uses a controlled atmosphere and a build-chamber temperature of approximately 600°C.
The proposed intervention is intended primarily for miniature geometries manufactured by powder bed fusion.
The optimal preheat temperature for AlCrFeNiSi has not been fully quantified.
The effect of preheating on phase evolution and microstructure in AlCrFeNiSi has not been fully quantified.
Residual-stress distributions can be compared between preheated and non-preheated builds using X-ray diffraction or another stress-mapping method.

The hypothesis is falsified if preheated specimens show neither statistically significant residual-stress reduction nor statistically significant mechanical-property improvement relative to non-preheated controls.
